full_judgment: 20. Thus, from the evidence of OPWs. 1-5, it appears that he made a consistent statement with other OPWs to the effect that case land was transferred much earlier by an oral gift than that of the deed under pre-emption and pre-emptee No.1 being the recipient of oral gift constructed her homestead long before the alleged execution and registration of the deed under pre-emption. Since nothing has been transferred by the deed under pre-emption, the application of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in the instant case is not maintainable against the said deed. Having regard upon those discussion of oral gift, sale deed, section 54 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1950 and section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, the High Court Division held that the impugned judgments and orders are although judgment of reversal, but those are nothing but per-verse one inasmuch as those were recorded without discussing and considering the material evidence on record and was recorded upon emotion.
